title: Congruence arithmetic and valid cancellation
terms: congruence; modulus; residue class; modular arithmetic; cancellation modulo n; Chinese remainder theorem.

exposition.text:
For n > 0, a ≡ b (mod n) means n | (a − b). Congruences may be added, subtracted, multi-
plied, and raised to nonnegative integer powers. Cancellation must track the modulus: ac ≡ bc
(mod n) implies a ≡ b (mod n/ gcd(c, n)), and preserves modulus n when c is a unit modulo n.
A useful extension is the Chinese remainder theorem: congruences with pairwise coprime mod-
uli specify exactly one residue class modulo their product. With moduli m, n that are not co-
prime, x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) is consistent exactly when a ≡ b (mod gcd(m, n)), and
then has one class modulo lcm(m, n).
A residue class a modulo m splits into exactly k classes modulo km: a, a + m, . . . , a + (k − 1)m.
CRT also combines independent root choices of polynomial congruences over coprime factors.
For a composite modulus, a product can be zero while neither factor is zero modulo that whole
modulus.

question.text:
What is the least positive integer x satisfying x ≡ 2 (mod 7) and x ≡ 5 (mod 11)?
(A) 16 (B) 23 (C) 38 (D) 49 (E) 60

solution.text:
−1
Write x = 2+ 7k. Then 7k ≡ 3 (mod 11), so k ≡ 2 (mod 11) because 7 ≡ 8. Hence x ≡ 16
(mod 77).

question.text:
For integers a, b, 18a ≡ 18b (mod 84) is equivalent to which condition?
(A) a ≡ b (mod 84) (B) a ≡ b (mod 42)
(C) a ≡ b (mod 28) (D) a ≡ b (mod 14)
(E) a ≡ b (mod 7)

solution.text:
The gcd of 18 and 84 is 6. Thus 84 | 18(a − b) is equivalent to 14 | 3(a − b) and, because 3 is
coprime to 14, to 14 | a − b.

question.text:
Which value of b makes the system x ≡ 5 (mod 12), x ≡ b (mod 18) consistent?
(A) 1 (B) 3 (C) 8 (D) 11 (E) 14

solution.text:
The gcd of the moduli is six. Compatibility requires b ≡ 5 (mod 6), and only eleven among
the choices has this residue. The resulting solution class is modulo the lcm thirty-six, not
the product two hundred sixteen.

question.text:
How many residue classes modulo 54 satisfy both x ≡ 2 (mod 6) and x ≡ 5 (mod 9)?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 6

solution.text:
The congruences are compatible modulo their common divisor three. Writing x = 2+6k gives
6k ≡ 3 (mod 9), so k ≡ 2 (mod 3) and x ≡ 14 (mod 18). Modulo fifty-four, this class lifts
to 14, 32, 50, giving three distinct classes.

How many residue classes modulo 15 solve x ≡ 1 (mod 15)?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 8

solution.text:
Modulo each of the primes three and five, x must be 1 or −1. The two sign choices are
independent under CRT, giving four classes modulo fifteen: 1, 4, 11, 14. Over a composite
modulus, (x − 1)(x + 1) ≡ 0 does not force one whole factor to vanish modulo the full
modulus.
